paras: The shooting of Will Jones took place on the evening of August 26, 1900, in Newton, Kansas, when the city marshal shot a Black man by that name in the leg as he ran from an accusation of theft. Jones survived, and the papers, relying on the officer's side, said he admitted stealing a watch. The case ran as a short wire item and as a one-line entry in a column of Kansas news.
According to a dispatch from Newton, the man gave his name as Will Jones and was accused of stealing a watch from 'a prominent citizen.' The Kansas papers gave his name as William Jones.

At about 7 o'clock that evening, Jones began to run when he was confronted about the theft. The city marshal, who is not named, ordered him to stop, and when he kept running the marshal shot him in the leg. The dispatch closed by saying that 'the negro admitted his guilt.'
The coverage does not say how serious the wound was, whether Jones was charged or tried, or whether anyone looked into the shooting.

The Arizona Republican carried the Newton dispatch on August 27 under the headline 'Newton Negro Thief Shot,' which called Jones a thief before the story said he had been accused. The dispatch gave only the marshal's version, and it presented the shot as the result of Jones's refusal to stop.

Later that week a syndicated column, 'Kansas Items of Interest,' reduced the story to one sentence describing 'a negro who confessed stealing a watch.' The same sentence ran in weeklies at Meade and Dodge City on August 30, Chanute on August 31, and Hays on September 1, placed between notes on volunteers, utility fees and congressional politics. No account of the shooting was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Shooting of Will Jones
bases: A city marshal shot a man in the leg when he ran from a theft accusation and refused an order to stop; no mob or crowd is mentioned (A1, A3).

The only reports are one wire dispatch (A1) and a Kansas news-column brief syndicated in identical words (A3, reprinted in A2, A4, A5), both giving only the marshal's side; they agree but are not clearly independent.

accounts.label: Wire report (marshal's version)
accounts.gist: Jones stole a watch from a prominent citizen, ran when accused, refused the marshal's command to stop, and was shot in the leg; he then admitted his guilt.

accounts.label: Kansas news-column brief
accounts.gist: William Jones, 'a negro who confessed stealing a watch,' was chased by the Newton marshal and shot in the leg when he refused to stop.

framing.detail: Headlined 'Newton Negro Thief Shot', the dispatch states the theft as fact, says Jones 'admitted his guilt,' and presents the shooting as a response to his refusal to stop.
Kansas weeklies ran a one-sentence item among state news, calling Jones 'a negro who confessed stealing a watch' without comment on the shooting.
